messages:
Sarah (Support): FYI incoming from AcmeHealth (acct 67342). Procurement is refusing to accept any invoice unless we have an *official signed PO* on file. They said legal blocks billing without it. They attached a scanned PO template but it's unsigned. Can we issue a proforma or hold credits while they get signature? Urgent — customer wants usage to continue. @Devon (Acct Rep) @Mike (Billing)

Devon (Acct Rep): Thanks — I pinged their procurement contact already (email pasted below). They say their internal process requires a purchase order number and signature before any invoice will be paid. Do we have any precedent issuing a proforma invoice that they can route internally for approval?

Mike (Billing): We don't normally generate a formal invoice without PO for enterprise accounts on Dedicated, but we can issue a proforma/quote PDF that mirrors the invoice line items. Proforma won't trigger accounting collection though. If they need an invoice number for internal routing we could create a draft with a note "Pending PO". Is that acceptable to them?

Sarah (Support): Their message: "our vendor onboarding policy: invoice only after PO is received. Please provide a signed PO or a pro-forma document with line items and total so we can raise an internal PO." They explicitly asked for "a doc we can attach to our PO request." Sounds like proforma would help.

Anna (Sales Ops): From a contract perspective: account has standard TOS and an executed SOW. No special PO clause. Customer on Dedicated commit, so we need to ensure usage is covered. If they refuse to pay until PO is in place we can hold billing but we should avoid service interruption. Customer asked for: company name, remit address, tax/VAT ID, description of services, period (Jan 1–31), and total.

Mike (Billing): Ok — I can generate a proforma PDF with those fields. Need the following to match their procurement intake:
- Remit name: Redwood Inference, Inc.
- Address: 123 Inference Way, San Francisco, CA 94107
- VAT/Tax ID: US-EIN 12-3456789
- Line items: "Redwood Dedicated - Jan 2026 usage" qty 1, unit price $15,000, total $15,000
- Note: "Proforma — subject to issuance of official PO. Will issue final invoice upon receipt of PO."

Lindsay (Eng): Quick note — nothing to change on runtime. No auto-shutdown scheduled. Reconfirming we shouldn't hit quota enforcement while this is resolved. Ops team: please avoid automated billing-based throttles for acct 67342 for 72h.

Devon (Acct Rep): Customer contact confirmed they'd accept proforma as input to their procurement cycle, but they want our finance contact to sign off. @Mike (Billing) can you attach a digital signature or will a printed-scan suffice?

Mike (Billing): I can sign the proforma (electronic signature). I'll include a signature block: "Mike Reynolds, Billing Manager" and generate PDF. I'll also copy accounting@redwood.com. Once I upload, I'll share a download link and ask the customer to attach it to their PO request.

billing-bot: New proforma generated for acct 67342 by Mike Reynolds at 2026-01-12T14:10:05Z — link: https://files.redwood.internal/proforma/67342-20260112.pdf :paperclip:

Sarah (Support): Sent the proforma to the procurement contact. They acknowledged receipt and said it'll go into their 5-business-day approval queue. They reiterated that final invoice will only be issued after PO number is supplied.

Devon (Acct Rep): I'll follow up in 3 business days and escalate to their procurement lead if no PO number received. Also asked legal if we can apply billing hold without breaking commit terms — they said we should avoid service interruption and instead hold invoicing until PO arrives.

Mike (Billing): Noted. I'll label the billing run as "pending PO - do not finalize" for this account. If PO arrives, we'll backdate invoice to the service period. If they never supply PO, we'll proceed per contract terms after 30 days.

Sarah (Support): Thanks team. I'll mark this thread solved for now and reopen if procurement asks for additional fields (e.g., country-specific VAT lines). :thumbsup:
